design_detail: Meta-analysis of (C)BT studies and pharmacological studies for GAD, with comparison of effect sizes across therapy types and subset of direct-comparison studies
comparison_group: Control conditions; pharmacotherapy (indirect and direct comparisons)
population: Patients with generalized anxiety disorder (non-perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 65 (C)BT and pharmacological studies included; pooled participant total not reported in abstract
rationale: PubMed type Meta-Analysis; abstract says 65 (C)BT and pharmacological studies were included. Component study designs and pooled N are not stated in the abstract.

design_detail: Canadian Task Force on Preventive Health Care recommendation statement on depression screening in adults
population: Adults (general population; screening recommendations)
sample_size_detail: Guideline; no sample size applicable
rationale: Title 'Recommendations on screening for depression in adults' and PubMed type Practice Guideline. File contains metadata only (no abstract in PubMed).

design_detail: RANZCOG best practice statement (C-Obs 48) on perinatal mental health care
population: Perinatal women (professional college guidance)
sample_size_detail: Best practice statement; no sample size applicable
rationale: Citation describes a college 'Best practice statement' on perinatal mental health care; not indexed in PubMed, citation only.

design_detail: Journal article (J Reprod Infant Psychol 2012) on patient-, provider-, and system-level barriers and facilitators to addressing perinatal depression; not indexed in PubMed, design not determinable from citation
severity_measure: Title indicates a barriers/facilitators paper, not a treatment-outcome comparison; design unknown
population: Patients, providers, and systems involved in perinatal depression care (details unknown)
sample_size_detail: Not reported (citation only)
rationale: Coded from the ACOG citation alone, per the coordinator's correction (the earlier file held the wrong PubMed abstract). The title doesn't show whether this is a qualitative study, survey, or review, so it is coded Other.

design_detail: Online webinar/training course (ACOG webinars platform) by UMass Chan Medical School
population: Obstetric clinicians (training resource)
sample_size_detail: Training resource; no sample size applicable
rationale: Citation is an online course URL (pathlms.com/acogwebinars) on addressing perinatal mental health conditions; a training program, not a study.

design_detail: Cross-sectional survey of ACOG Fellows on prenatal depression screening and antidepressant prescribing
population: US obstetrician-gynecologists (ACOG Fellows) providing prenatal care
sample_size_detail: 1000 Fellows surveyed; 379 responded (37.9%); 288 provided care to pregnant patients and answered the depression/antidepressant questions
rationale: Survey 'distributed to a sample of 1000 Fellows' describing ob-gyn practices and opinions; no comparative effect estimate. Analytic N is the 288 respondents caring for pregnant patients.

design_detail: Planned secondary analysis of a prospective cohort (abstract calls it retrospective cohort), single US academic center (Northwestern), pre- vs post-implementation of perinatal collaborative care model; propensity score covariate adjustment with race-by-epoch interaction; no concurrent control
severity_measure: Propensity score included maternal age, insurance, parity, tobacco, substance use history, chronic medical problem, and any mental health history (presence of diagnosis only); postpartum models added GDM and preterm birth
comparison_group: Pre-implementation epoch (2015-2016); Black vs White individuals within epochs
population: Black and White pregnant/postpartum people receiving prenatal care at Northwestern Medicine-affiliated practices, deliveries 2015-2019
sample_size_detail: 2286 pre-implementation (262 Black, 2024 White) and 2424 post-implementation (313 Black, 2111 White); treatment-recommendation analyses limited to those screening positive
rationale: Pre/post epoch comparison without a concurrent untreated control, so not quasi-experimental per protocol; propensity score covariate adjustment. Covariates include only 'any maternal chronic somatic medical problem or mental health history', with no severity measure.

design_detail: Program description and utilization/cost report of the Massachusetts Child Psychiatry Access Project (MCPAP) for Moms, first 18 months
population: Massachusetts obstetric practices and perinatal women served by MCPAP for Moms
sample_size_detail: First 18 months: 87 Ob/Gyn practices enrolled, 100 trainings, 1123 women served; cost estimate based on 71618 annual deliveries
rationale: Describes development, implementation, and outcomes (enrollment, encounter volume, cost) of a population-based program with no comparison group or effect estimate.

design_detail: Cross-sectional analysis of nationally representative US survey data 2005-2009 (NSDUH per study description), pregnant vs nonpregnant women with past-year MDE; chi-square and adjusted prevalence ratios
severity_measure: aPRs reported but covariates not listed in abstract; all women met criteria for past-year MDE (restriction on diagnosis)
comparison_group: Nonpregnant women of reproductive age with past-year MDE
population: US women aged 18-44 with past-year major depressive episode, 2005-2009 national survey data
sample_size_detail: 375 pregnant and 8657 nonpregnant women with past-year MDE
rationale: Non-randomized comparison (pregnancy status) with 'adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR)'; adjustment set not described in the abstract, so severity is Unclear and coded as excl. severity by default.

design_detail: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of double-blind RCTs of 21 antidepressants vs placebo or head-to-head for acute MDD
population: Adults (18+) with major depressive disorder (non-perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 522 double-blind parallel RCTs comprising 116477 participants (1979-2016)
rationale: Searched for 'double-blind, randomised controlled trials' and excluded quasi-randomised trials; included 522 trials with 116477 participants.

design_detail: Systematic review, random-effects meta-analysis, and network meta-analysis of retrospective cohort and case-control studies of SSRI/SNRI exposure in pregnancy and PPHN
comparison_group: Offspring of women unexposed to SSRIs/SNRIs; between-SSRI comparisons in NMA
population: Pregnant women and their newborns
sample_size_detail: 11 studies; 156978 women and offspring exposed to SSRIs/SNRIs (total including unexposed not reported); 452 exposed PPHN cases
rationale: Eligible designs were 'Retrospective cohort studies and case-control studies'; 11 studies included. Only the exposed count (156978) is given, not total pooled participants, so sample_size_n is null.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (comparative effectiveness) of antidepressant treatment for depression in pregnancy and postpartum
comparison_group: Other antidepressants, placebo or no treatment, nondrug treatments
population: Pregnant or postpartum women with depression and their children
sample_size_detail: 6 RCTs and 15 observational studies; pooled participant total not reported
rationale: 'Six randomized controlled trials and 15 observational studies provided evidence.' Total pooled N not reported in the abstract.

design_detail: Single-center, 6-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of flexible-dose sertraline (50-200 mg) after 1-week single-blind placebo lead-in
population: Women aged 18-45 with major depression onset within 3 months of delivery, New Haven/southern Connecticut, recruited 1994-2004
sample_size_detail: 38 entered placebo lead-in; 36 randomized (17 sertraline, 19 placebo) = ITT sample; 33 evaluable (>=3 post-randomization assessments); 27 met strict DSM-IV 4-week onset criteria
rationale: 'A total of 17 women were randomized to the sertraline group and 19 ... to placebo'; primary analysis compared response rates in the ITT sample (n = 36).

design_detail: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of placebo- and active-controlled randomised trials of drugs for GAD
population: Adult outpatients with generalised anxiety disorder (non-perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 89 trials; 25441 patients randomly assigned to 22 active drugs or placebo
rationale: Network meta-analysis 'on randomised trials in adult outpatients with generalised anxiety disorder'; 89 trials, 25441 patients.

design_detail: Clinical narrative review of treatment of peripartum bipolar disorder (screening, illness and medication risks, dosing, nondrug treatments)
population: Perinatal women with bipolar disorder (review)
sample_size_detail: Narrative review; no sample size
rationale: PubMed type 'Review' in Obstet Gynecol Clin North Am; the full text is a clinical overview with no search strategy or systematic methods.

design_detail: Danish national register linkage (Medical Birth Register and Psychiatric Central Register), 1973-1993; psychosis admission rates within 91 days after delivery compared with non-puerperal women, reported as relative risks for all, first, and readmissions
severity_measure: Abstract reports RRs but never says whether they are adjusted or standardized (Amendment 1 rule b); exposure is childbirth, not a treatment
comparison_group: Non-puerperal women in the general Danish female population
population: Danish women, 1973-1993 (postpartum women vs non-puerperal women)
sample_size_detail: 1253 psychosis admissions within 91 days after delivery; denominator population size not reported in abstract
rationale: Abstract reports relative risks of admission after delivery compared with non-puerperal women but never says whether they are adjusted, so per Amendment 1 rule (b) it is coded unadjusted/descriptive with severity Unclear. The unit (admissions) is also not a person-level analytic N.

design_detail: Two-part paper: review of 8 published cohort studies (hypothesis generation) plus population-based case-control study in EUROCAT Antiepileptic Study Database (19 European congenital anomaly registries, 1995-2005) testing 5 specific malformations; malformed controls; logistic regression
severity_measure: ORs adjusted for maternal age, year of birth, and (for no-AED comparison) reporting registry; no measure of epilepsy severity (e.g., seizure type/frequency)
comparison_group: Fetuses unexposed to AEDs; valproic acid monotherapy; other AED monotherapy (controls = non-chromosomal and chromosomal malformation registrations)
population: Registrations of major congenital malformations (live births, fetal deaths >=20 wk, terminations) in 19 European registries covering 3.8 million births, 1995-2005
sample_size_detail: Case-control: 11790 cases in 5 malformation subgroups, 69883 non-chromosomal controls, 11763 chromosomal controls (93436 total); 131 carbamazepine-monotherapy-exposed registrations. Literature review: 8 cohort studies, 2680 carbamazepine-exposed pregnancies
rationale: Coded on the hypothesis-testing case-control analysis, which yields the main ORs; the review of 8 cohort studies only generated 'indications' to test. ORs 'adjusted for year of birth and maternal age' (plus registry), with no severity measure. Medium confidence because the paper is also indexed as a Systematic Review.

design_detail: Multicenter prospective observational pharmacokinetic study with frequent blood sampling before and early in pregnancy; population mixed-effects modeling of lamotrigine clearance vs gestational week and estradiol
comparison_group: Within-person preconception baseline; low vs high clearance-change groups
population: Pregnant women with epilepsy on lamotrigine without interacting medications
sample_size_detail: 25 pregnancies in 22 participants
rationale: Outcome is lamotrigine clearance (LTG-CL/F) and its relation to estradiol and gestational week, a drug-concentration study with no clinical outcome comparison.

design_detail: Prospective pharmacokinetic study of lamotrigine concentrations sampled preconception and monthly through pregnancy and postpartum
population: Women with epilepsy on lamotrigine monotherapy
sample_size_detail: 14 women on lamotrigine monotherapy
rationale: Measured lamotrigine apparent and weight-adjusted clearance across trimesters vs preconception baseline; a clearance study.

design_detail: Pharmacokinetic study of lamotrigine apparent clearance at preconception, each trimester, and postpartum (ANOVA, paired t-tests)
population: Pregnant women treated with lamotrigine with complete steady-state data
sample_size_detail: 12 pregnancies with complete steady-state data before, during, and after pregnancy
rationale: Evaluated 'changes in lamotrigine (LTG) clearance before, during, and after pregnancy' in 12 pregnancies; a dose-requirement/clearance study.

design_detail: Prospective observational study of placental passage (umbilical cord-to-maternal plasma ratio) of atypical antipsychotics/haloperidol at delivery, with descriptive obstetric outcomes
comparison_group: Between-drug comparison of placental passage ratios; no unexposed group
population: Pregnant women with laboratory-confirmed antipsychotic use proximate to delivery
sample_size_detail: 54 women included in analysis; complete maternal-infant sample pairs for 50
rationale: Primary aim was to 'quantify placental permeability' via cord-to-maternal concentration ratios; obstetric outcomes are only descriptive.

design_detail: 8-week multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of quetiapine 600 or 300 mg/day (BOLDER I)
population: Outpatients with bipolar I or II disorder in a major depressive episode (non-perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 542 randomized (360 bipolar I, 182 bipolar II); number analyzed not given in abstract
rationale: 'Five hundred forty-two outpatients ... were randomly assigned' to quetiapine or placebo.

design_detail: 8-week multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of quetiapine 300 or 600 mg/day (BOLDER II); ANCOVA/LOCF primary analysis
population: Patients with bipolar I or II disorder in a depressive episode (non-perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 509 randomized; 59% completed the study
rationale: 'Of 509 patients randomized, 59% completed the study'; double-blind placebo-controlled RCT.

design_detail: 8-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of quetiapine 300 or 600 mg/day and lithium monotherapy (EMBOLDEN I; NCT00206141)
population: Adults with bipolar I or II disorder in an acute major depressive episode (non-perinatal), 2005-2007
sample_size_detail: 802 randomized: quetiapine 300 mg (n=265), quetiapine 600 mg (n=268), lithium (n=136), placebo (n=133)
rationale: '802 patients ... were randomly allocated' to quetiapine, lithium, or placebo.

design_detail: Systematic review of systematic reviews (umbrella review) of lurasidone for bipolar depression; AMSTAR/R-AMSTAR quality appraisal; narrative synthesis, no meta-analysis
comparison_group: None (narrative synthesis of reviews of lurasidone vs placebo/other agents)
population: Patients with bipolar depression (non-perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 12 systematic reviews included; no pooled participant count
rationale: 'Only systematic reviews were included'; reviews of RCTs and of observational studies were both eligible, and the actual mix of primary designs is not stated, so components are coded Not stated.

design_detail: Single case report of lurasidone serum concentrations and bipolar disorder course from second trimester to 3 months postpartum
population: Primiparous woman with bipolar disorder treated with lurasidone
sample_size_detail: One patient
rationale: 'This case report presents perinatal changes in the concentration of lurasidone' in one woman; PubMed type Case Reports.

design_detail: Prospective study of infants exposed to valproic acid (mono- and polytherapy) compared with matched-pair controls and controls from a larger AED study; also maternal VPA serum levels
severity_measure: Matched-pair controls used but matching variables not described in abstract; no epilepsy severity measure mentioned
comparison_group: 26 matched-pair controls and 116 controls from a larger antiepileptic drug study
population: Infants of women with epilepsy receiving valproic acid during pregnancy (Germany)
sample_size_detail: 26 VPA-exposed infants (14 monotherapy, 12 combination therapy), 26 matched-pair controls, 116 additional controls
rationale: Exposed infants were compared with '26 matched-pair controls and 116 controls', so the design involves matching (coded adjusted); matching factors and any severity measure can't be determined from the abstract.

design_detail: Lancet research letter (PubMed: Comparative Study; Letter) on in-utero valproate exposure and neural tube defects; design details not available
severity_measure: No abstract or text in file; analysis and any adjustment unknown
comparison_group: Unclear (presumably pregnancies not exposed to valproate)
population: Pregnancies exposed to valproate (details not available)
sample_size_detail: Not reported in file (no abstract)
rationale: File has metadata only (no abstract in PubMed). The 'Comparative Study' tag on a 1986 letter suggests a crude group comparison, but design, adjustment, and N can't be verified.

design_detail: Prospective multinational cohort (Japan, Italy, Canada) of offspring of mothers with epilepsy; malformation incidence by AED, dose, level, and polytherapy; background risk factors examined
severity_measure: Abstract reports crude incidences by drug, dose, and number of AEDs; says background factors were studied but does not describe a multivariable model or covariates
comparison_group: Offspring without AED exposure; between-AED comparisons
population: Offspring of mothers with epilepsy in Japan, Italy, and Canada
sample_size_detail: 983 offspring analyzed prospectively; exposed vs unexposed counts not given in abstract
rationale: Main results are malformation incidences (e.g., 3.1% unexposed vs 9.0% exposed) and dose correlations. The abstract says malformations were not associated with 'any background factors studied', but doesn't show whether drug estimates were adjusted.

design_detail: Letter reporting case(s) of valproic acid teratogenicity (PubMed: Case Reports; Letter)
population: Infant(s) exposed to valproic acid in utero
sample_size_detail: Number of cases not reported in file (no abstract)
rationale: PubMed publication types 'Case Reports; Letter'; no abstract in file, so the number of cases is unknown.

design_detail: Case series describing dysmorphic features in infants exposed to valproate in utero
population: Infants exposed to sodium valproate/valproic acid during pregnancy (UK)
sample_size_detail: Four exposed infants (three surviving)
rationale: 'Four infants who were exposed to sodium valproate or valproic acid during pregnancy are described'; no comparison group.

design_detail: Single case report of a male with fetal valproate syndrome and autism
population: Child with prenatal valproate exposure
sample_size_detail: One patient
rationale: 'We report on a patient' with a phenotype compatible with fetal valproate syndrome and autism; PubMed type Case Reports.

design_detail: Prospective follow-up (Finland, per authorship) comparing cognitive/motor function at 5.5 years in children of mothers with epilepsy vs control children; within-group analysis of maternal seizure type, seizures in pregnancy, paternal education, and AED exposure
severity_measure: Within the epilepsy group, maternal partial seizures and seizures during pregnancy were examined alongside AED exposure, but the abstract does not say whether this was a multivariable model
comparison_group: Control children of mothers without epilepsy
population: Children (age 5.5 years) of mothers with epilepsy, 89% AED-exposed in utero, and control children, all with normal general intelligence
sample_size_detail: 104 children of epileptic mothers and 105 control children
rationale: The primary contrast (study vs control children) appears to be a crude comparison. Within-group risk factors included seizure-related severity proxies alongside AED exposure, but whether these were jointly modeled can't be determined from the abstract.

design_detail: 1970 Lancet article on neonatal coagulation defect after maternal anticonvulsant treatment; design not determinable from file (no abstract)
severity_measure: No abstract or text in file
population: Neonates of mothers treated with anticonvulsants during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: Not reported in file (no abstract)
rationale: File contains only the title and PubMed type 'Journal Article' (no abstract), so the design (case series, physiologic study, or comparison) can't be determined. Coded Other for that reason.

design_detail: Meta-analysis (MOOSE-guided, PubMed/Embase 1999-2011) of clinical trials reporting weight change on antipsychotics, stratified by drug and duration of exposure; meta-regression for duration
comparison_group: Placebo; other antipsychotics (pre-post weight change per arm)
population: Adults (18+) treated with antipsychotics, any diagnosis (non-perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 307 included studies (257 reporting weight change; 39 in AP-naive patients); pooled participant total not reported
rationale: Inclusion allowed 'Randomised controlled trial, controlled clinical trial or clinical trial or phase IV' trials, so components are RCTs plus non-randomized trials (coded Mixed). 307 studies; no total N reported.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis of MetS prevalence in severe mental illness, with relative-risk meta-analyses vs diagnostic groups and matched general-population controls and meta-regression of moderators
comparison_group: Other SMI diagnoses; antipsychotic-naive participants; matched general population controls
population: People with schizophrenia/related psychoses, bipolar disorder, or major depressive disorder (non-perinatal)
sample_size_detail: Pooled MetS prevalence from 198 studies with n = 52678
rationale: Systematic review and meta-analysis with pooled prevalence 'N = 198; n = 52,678'; component study designs not stated in the abstract.

design_detail: Two population-based retrospective cohort studies (UK THIN and Hong Kong CDARS) of antipsychotic continuers vs discontinuers among prior users, propensity score fine-stratification weighting; plus updated meta-analysis
severity_measure: Propensity score covariates not listed in abstract; restriction to women with pre-pregnancy antipsychotic use (active-comparator: continuers vs discontinuers)
comparison_group: Women prescribed antipsychotics before pregnancy who discontinued during pregnancy
population: Nondiabetic women with antipsychotic prescriptions before first registered pregnancy, UK THIN and Hong Kong CDARS
sample_size_detail: 3114 women with first pregnancies (2351 THIN, 763 CDARS); continuer/discontinuer split not given in abstract
rationale: Primary analysis is the cohort comparison using 'Propensity Score fine-stratification weighting'; covariates are not listed in the abstract, so severity is Unclear and coded excl. severity by default. Restricting to first pregnancies rules out a within-mother comparison.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies of GDM risk by preconception mental disorder (mood, anxiety, psychotic, eating disorders)
comparison_group: Women without the preconception mental disorder
population: Pregnant women with and without preconception mental disorders
sample_size_detail: 22 observational studies (mostly retrospective cohorts); pooled participant total not reported
rationale: '22 observational studies met inclusion criteria'; pooled ORs by disorder; no total N in abstract.

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of case-control, cohort, and interventional studies of lithium safety and efficacy in pregnancy and postpartum
comparison_group: Unexposed pregnancies / disease-matched or general controls; no lithium for relapse prevention
population: Pregnant and postpartum women (mainly with bipolar disorder) and their offspring
sample_size_detail: 29 studies included, 13 in quantitative analysis; outcome-specific pooled N: any congenital anomaly N=23300 (k=11), cardiac anomalies N=1348475 (k=12), spontaneous abortion N=1289 (k=3), postpartum relapse N=48 (k=2); no overall total
rationale: Included 'case-control, cohort, and interventional studies', with Newcastle-Ottawa and Cochrane risk-of-bias tools, so coded Mixed. No single total pooled N; outcome-specific Ns are in the detail field.

design_detail: Prospective longitudinal pharmacokinetic study with serial 12-/24-hour blood and urine sampling each trimester and postpartum (NCT02490241); lithium elimination clearance, creatinine clearance, and mood ratings
population: Pregnant women with bipolar disorder continuing lithium, Northwestern University, Chicago
sample_size_detail: 3 women completed serial sampling protocols
rationale: Characterizes 'lithium elimination clearance' across pregnancy and postpartum in 3 women; a PK study with no comparison group.

design_detail: Systematic review (PubMed 1995-2015) of case reports, case series, and prospective/cross-sectional studies of mood stabilizers during breastfeeding (RID, milk-to-plasma ratio, infant levels, adverse events)
population: Breastfed infants of lactating women taking mood stabilizers
sample_size_detail: 26 reports: lamotrigine 122 cases (12 reports), lithium 26 (5), carbamazepine 64 (5), valproate 9 (3), oxcarbazepine 2 (2); no overall total stated
rationale: Systematic PubMed search with 26 of 604 reports included; eligible designs were case reports, case series, and prospective or cross-sectional studies. Case counts are given per drug only.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Kaiser Permanente Washington EHR linked to Washington State birth records, singleton live births 2001-2014; restricted to prior antidepressant users; continuers vs discontinuers; IPTW with GEE (Poisson) for GDM
severity_measure: IPTW included psychotherapy visits, psychiatry visits, inpatient psychiatric hospitalization, and other psychotropic fills (antipsychotic, benzodiazepine, mood stabilizer), plus mental health diagnoses; PHQ-9 described but not modeled
comparison_group: Women with pre-pregnancy antidepressant fills who discontinued during pregnancy
population: Births to women aged 15-45 without pre-existing diabetes, enrolled in KPWA, with an antidepressant fill in the 6 months before pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 2845 births for GDM analysis: 1634 continuers, 1211 discontinuers; blood glucose analysis 1101 births (613 vs 488)
rationale: IPTW accounted for 'mental health conditions and indicators of mental health severity'. Table 1 covariates include inpatient psychiatric hospitalization, psychiatry visits, and other psychotropic fills. GEE accounted for repeat births but there was no sibling contrast.
